## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 2: adjust in the **outcome model**
- Today: model the **treatment assignment** instead, and build **comparable groups** before looking at the outcome
- By the end you can:
  - estimate a **propensity score** and check **overlap**
  - **match** and check **balance**
  - estimate the effect in the matched sample
:::

# Topic 1 — The propensity score {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Probability of enrolment

```{r}
ps_model <- glm(f_ps, data = htn, family = binomial)
htn$ps <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")
htn |> group_by(programme) |> summarise(min = round(min(ps), 2), mean = round(mean(ps), 2), max = round(max(ps), 2))
```

::: {.incremental}
- **Propensity score** = P(enrolled | confounders). Two adults with the **same score** have, on average, the **same confounder distribution**: like a small randomised trial
- Include the **confounders** (and predictors of the outcome); **not** mediators, colliders or variables that only predict enrolment
- The aim is **balance**, not prediction: do **not** judge it by the AUC
:::

## Overlap (positivity)

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-height: 4.2
ggplot(htn, aes(ps, fill = factor(programme, labels = c("Not enrolled", "Enrolled")))) + geom_density(alpha = 0.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = c(col_blue, col_red)) + labs(x = "Propensity score", fill = NULL)
```

::: {.key}
The two distributions **overlap** over almost the whole range: for nearly every enrolled adult there are **comparable** non-enrolled adults. Regions **without** overlap cannot be compared without **extrapolation**.
:::

# Topic 2 — Matching {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Balance before matching

```{r}
bal.tab(f_ps, data = htn, un = TRUE, s.d.denom = "pooled")$Balance[, "Diff.Un", drop = FALSE] |> round(2)
```

**Standardised mean difference (SMD)**: difference in means divided by the SD. **Below 0.1** is the usual target. Here **baseline SBP 0.63** and **age 0.43**: far off.

## 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching

```{r}
m_out <- matchit(f_ps, data = htn, method = "nearest", distance = "glm", caliper = 0.2)
m_out
```

::: {.incremental}
- Each enrolled adult is paired with the **non-enrolled adult with the closest score**; the **caliper** (0.2 SD) refuses poor matches
- **2,114 adults (1,057 pairs)** remain; **172 enrolled** adults found no match
- No outcome data are used: the design is fixed **before** looking at SBP
:::

## Balance after matching

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-height: 4.4
love.plot(m_out, thresholds = 0.1, abs = TRUE, stars = "raw")
```

```{r}
bal.tab(m_out, un = TRUE)$Balance[c("age", "diabetes", "baseline_sbp"), c("Diff.Un", "Diff.Adj")] |> round(2)
```

::: {.key}
All SMDs are now **below 0.1** (baseline SBP 0.63 → 0.06). Judge matching by **balance**, never by p-values. If balance is poor, **change the propensity model** (add interactions, curves) and match again.
:::

# Topic 3 — The effect {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## In the matched sample

```{r}
md <- match.data(m_out)
fit_m <- lm(sbp_12m ~ programme, data = md, weights = weights)
round(coeftest(fit_m, vcov. = vcovCL, cluster = ~subclass)["programme", 1:2], 2)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **−5.9 mmHg** (SE 0.51): close to the regression estimate
- SE **clustered on the matched pair**
- Matching the enrolled targets the **ATT**, here for the **enrolled who could be matched**: say so, and describe who was **dropped**
- Adding the covariates to this model ("double adjustment") removes residual imbalance
:::

## Strengths and limits

| Strength | Limit |
|---|---|
| Separates **design** from **outcome analysis** | Only **measured** confounders are balanced |
| **Balance** is visible and checkable | Discards unmatched people (precision, target population) |
| Easy to explain | Many choices (caliper, ratio, replacement): **pre-specify** |

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z3q1", "What is a propensity score?",
         c("The probability of the outcome, given the exposure and the measured confounders",
           "The number of confounders on which two adults in the data agree exactly",
           "The share of the outcome variance that the exposure explains in the model",
           "The probability of receiving the exposure, given the measured confounders"), answer = 4,
         explain = "The propensity score summarises the measured confounders into one number: the chance of being exposed. Adults with the same score are comparable on those confounders.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z3q2", "How should you judge whether propensity-score matching has worked?",
         c("By covariate balance, e.g. standardised differences below 0.1",
           "By the AUC of the propensity model, which should be above 0.8",
           "By the p-value of the exposure in the matched outcome model",
           "By the number of adults that are kept in the matched sample"), answer = 1,
         explain = "The purpose of the score is to balance confounders between groups. A high AUC can even signal poor overlap.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z3q3", "The propensity distributions of the two groups hardly overlap. What does this mean?",
         c("The propensity model is correct, as it discriminates well between the two groups",
           "Some adults have no comparable counterpart, so their effect is not estimable",
           "The exposure has a strong effect on the outcome in most adults of the cohort",
           "Matching will work especially well, because the two groups are so distinct"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Without overlap (positivity) the comparison relies on extrapolation. The honest options are to restrict the population or to accept that the effect is not identified there.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z3q4", "In 1:1 matching, 172 enrolled adults found no match within the caliper. What is the consequence?",
         c("The estimate is biased by the caliper, which should therefore be removed",
           "The 172 adults should be matched to the nearest adult, whatever the distance",
           "Nothing follows, since dropped adults do not affect a matched analysis",
           "The estimate applies to the matched enrolled adults, a changed target"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Dropping unmatched adults protects comparability but changes who the result is about. Report how many were dropped and who they were.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("z3q5", "Which variables belong in the propensity-score model?",
         c("Confounders measured before the exposure, chosen from the DAG",
           "Mediators such as adherence, since they predict the outcome well",
           "Colliders such as clinic visits, since they predict enrolment well",
           "All the available variables, selected by a stepwise procedure"), answer = 1,
         explain = "The score must balance pre-exposure confounders. Post-exposure variables (mediators, colliders) bias the estimate, however well they predict.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- **Propensity score** = P(exposure | confounders)
- Check **overlap** (positivity) first
- **Match**, then check **balance** (SMD < 0.1, love plot)
- Estimate in the matched data with **pair-clustered SE**
- Matching targets the **ATT** and balances only **measured** confounders
:::
